name: Big Black
label: Touch and Go
lede: Steve Albini started Big Black alone at Northwestern with a drum machine, poached two guys from Naked Raygun, and spent six years making noise that was ugly on purpose and exact to the beat. Then he quit, on schedule, with the major labels at the door.

eras.title: One kid, one living room
eras.text: Steve Albini started Big Black as a solo project while a student at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois. He played everything himself, let a drum machine keep time, and sent the results out in packages meant to offend.

years.h: Albini records six songs in his living room, alone
years.p: Over spring break 1981 the Northwestern student plays guitar and bass over a drum machine. Touch and Go's own bio points out it wasn't his first band.

years.h: Lungs arrives with dollar bills and used condoms inside
years.p: The 1,500-copy EP comes out on Chicago's Ruthless Records. According to Wikipedia, the inserts also included Bruce Lee photos and bloodied paper.

eras.title: Borrowing from Naked Raygun
eras.text: Albini turned the project into a band by borrowing two members of Chicago's Naked Raygun. The rules were set early: no contracts, no advances, no manager, no booking agent, no lawyer. Big Black booked its own tours and paid its own bills.

years.h: Albini borrows two members of Naked Raygun
years.p: Singer Jeff Pezzati takes bass, and guitarist Santiago Durango comes over from the same band. [[Pat Byrne|6321b6f8-e574-480b-82d7-e5bf1a838fc5]], later of [[Urge Overkill|120e728a-4078-47b7-a31c-d581ade28bde]], plays real drums on the next record.

years.h: Bulldozer comes in a sleeve of sheet metal
years.p: The first 200 copies are galvanized metal, a nod to [[Public Image Ltd|68950696-ee9a-49b2-a8c2-d1d6c19355cc]]'s Metal Box. Albini later said he sorta conned Fever Records into paying for it.
years.xp: Iain Burgess engineered the EP. Cables is about a slaughterhouse in Montana, where Albini grew up, and Pigeon Kill about an Indiana town poisoning its pigeons. Most Big Black songs worked that way: short stories about the worst of America, many lifted from real events.

years.h: Big Black books its own first US tour
years.p: Nobody handles it but the band. The run sets up the records that would come out on Homestead.

years.h: Jeff Pezzati quits at the end of 1984
years.p: His day job and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]], the band he fronted, both needed him more.

eras.title: The Roland hits on one and three
eras.text: With Dave Riley on bass the line-up locked in, and the drum machine became the band's signature, programmed to hit the beats rock drummers leave alone. Big Black got louder and sharper, and fell out with the label selling its records. Chicago snubbed them at first, so they skipped Chicago, and Albini's badmouthing of the Metro got them banned there for good.

years.h: Racer-X comes out with no contract and no advance
years.p: Homestead's deal lets Big Black keep the rights to its recordings. This EP is the first record under it.

years.h: Dave Riley brings Detroit funk to the bass
years.p: Riley had worked at a Detroit studio where [[George Clinton|84683370-5eae-418b-acd8-883ac028a8a0]] and [[Sly Stone|a833e001-7c3b-491f-b7d4-2ef367837b95]] recorded. His low end gives Big Black a groove nobody expected.

years.h: A Rema-Rema cover rides free with Forced Exposure No. 9
years.p: Big Black plays the [[Rema-Rema|c34623b5-8d04-4b5b-87dc-2be531975d10]] song Rema-Rema on a 500-copy single packaged with the zine, where Albini also wrote.
years.xp: Albini's writing was its own provocation. His column in the Chicago zine Matter, Tired of Ugly Fat?, tore into the local scene and split readers down the middle.

years.big: We didn't want our audience milked for extra money to buy an alternate format.
years.h: Homestead sells the free Il Duce promos
years.p: Homestead asked for 500 12-inch copies of Il Duce to give to radio, on condition they not be sold. Steve Albini found them in shops as collector's items, called posing as a buyer, and was offered some, "but not in Chicago." That was his explanation for walking.
years.xp:
The break also ended Big Black's relationship with Homestead's distributor, Dutch East India Trading. For a band whose business model was a handshake, selling the promos was the one unforgivable move.

Big Black's last records came out on Touch and Go, run by Albini's close friend [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]].

years.cap: Santiago Durango, Steve Albini and Dave Riley, 1986
years.h: Roland, a TR-606, gets billed as a band member
years.p: It's programmed to accent beats one and three instead of rock's two and four. Club soundmen feared it would blow their speakers, and the band sometimes had to coerce the owner or threaten to cancel the show.
years.xp:
Albini never apologized for the machine. "In Big Black, the drum machine got to stretch its legs a little," he told Rolling Stone in 2014.

It didn't last: "The housing for it broke and all the components under the pads have deteriorated to the point that it's unusable."

years.h: Atomizer sells 3,000 copies, more than anyone expected
years.p: Big Black's first full-length, on Homestead, has Kerosene, Jordan, Minnesota and Bazooka Joe.
years.xp:
Jordan, Minnesota is about the 1983 child sex abuse scandal in that town. Live, Albini acted out the victim's part while the band stretched the noise out. Durango's verdict, in Rolling Stone: "It was unsettling." The records also drew accusations of racism and homophobia over slurs in the lyrics; Albini defended them as satire, and critics didn't all buy it.

When [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] picked Albini to produce In Utero, Atomizer was one of the records he cited, along with Albini's work on the Pixies and the Breeders.

years.h: The British press goes for Big Black before America does
years.p: Blast First, a label [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] recommended to Albini, handles the band in Europe, and the 1986 tour earns raves in the British music papers.

years.h: The Hammer Party puts Lungs and Bulldozer on one record
years.p: Homestead issues it in November, after Big Black has already left the label.

eras.title: Quit while they're loudest
eras.text: Big Black planned its own ending a year out: Santiago Durango was going to law school, so the band scheduled a final year of records and tours. Major labels came calling; Riley said the money would have meant it wasn't Big Black anymore.

years.big: I was tired of working shitty jobs just so that I could be in a band.
years.h: Law school gives Big Black an end date
years.p: Santiago Durango is headed to law school in fall 1987, and the band decides to stop rather than replace him. Durango explained his side to Rolling Stone, above. They spend the year finishing everything.
years.xp:
Durango said the band had run out of road: "I was just tapped out," and "a finite number of ideas" were left to explore as Big Black.

Albini had no regrets: "Ending that band was one of the most satisfying things I've ever done."

years.h: Headache arrives in a body bag
years.p: Touch and Go's first Big Black record has forensic photos of an accident victim on the cover and a sticker warning buyers that it isn't as good as Atomizer.
years.xp: The limited first edition came in a black plastic body bag. The sticker reads: "Not as good as Atomizer, so don't get your hopes up, cheese!"

years.h: Wire, Cheap Trick and Kraftwerk get the Big Black treatment
years.p: Touch and Go releases the Heartbeat single, a [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] cover, and He's a Whore / The Model, covering [[Cheap Trick|9f870653-72b0-4c6d-8c59-439a95963e09]] and [[Kraftwerk|5700dcd4-c139-4f31-aa3e-6382b9af9032]] with guitars playing the synth parts.
years.xp: On picking Kraftwerk's The Model, Albini said it "seemed like the perfect one" for adapting to a rock band.

years.h: Big Black plays Pukkelpop on Albini's 25th birthday
years.p: The Belgian festival is on July 22, with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] on the bill.

yt: Steve Albini on drugs and drinking in Big Black
years.h: Dave Riley smashes the drum machine at CBGB
years.p: Per Wikipedia's account of the breakup, Riley's drinking was ruining shows, and at a key CBGB gig he drunkenly smashed the Roland.
years.xp: Albini's list of complaints included lateness to rehearsals, always needing rides, and "flashes of brilliance offset by flashes of belligerence."

years.h: Wire's Bruce Gilbert and Graham Lewis crash the London encore
years.p: At a sold-out 1,300-capacity show, they join Big Black for Heartbeat, [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]]'s own song. Tapes from the London dates became Pigpile.

years.h: Big Black plays its last show in an abandoned Seattle power plant
years.p: Georgetown Steam Plant, no electricity, portable generators. The set ends with smashed instruments and explosives. In the room: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]], [[Mark Arm|3f99d2df-8859-4249-8a70-84fe04c5a096]], [[Kim Thayil|dd676aae-658e-42f3-b3d9-8660ea29198d]] and Sub Pop's [[Bruce Pavitt|f5230572-06e4-453c-a1dd-7a4b560da3bb]].
years.xp:
Producer Larry Reid explained the power: the plant "was then totally without electrical service, so we had to employ portable generators." Roland Barker and James Husted played synths from the catwalks, and poet Jesse Bernstein read before Big Black came on. Pavitt wrote that he cut his hand grabbing a piece of broken guitar.

Albini later called it "one of the oddest places that we played." He mixed the concert film, The Last Blast, and Cobain is visible in it at 31:14.

q: We wanted to make filthy music.
years.h: Songs About Fucking arrives with the band already finished
years.p: Side one, Happy Otter, was recorded in London; side two, Sad Otter, in Chicago on gear that became Electrical Audio. The first pressing of 8,000 makes it Big Black's best seller.
years.xp:
Albini on the title: "The term 'rock & roll music' originally meant dirty songs about fucking." Durango called it "the biggest 'fuck you' to the music industry that I am aware of." Blast First, the British label, bristled at the phrase.

The cover art came from Japanese manga a friend imported. Australia's Au Go Go label covered it with a sticker reading Please remove, which Albini said "would encourage petty vandalism in record stores." Robert Christgau marveled that the band could crush the competition and quit at the same time.

years.h: The Rich Man's Eight Track Tape puts Atomizer on CD
years.p: Touch and Go's CD adds Headache and the Heartbeat single, for a format Big Black never recorded for.

eras.title: Everybody goes somewhere else
eras.text: The members scattered in very different directions. Albini became the most famous recording engineer in independent music, Durango a lawyer, and Riley's life was upended by a stroke. Big Black's catalog stayed with Touch and Go.

years.h: Albini forms Rapeman, then engineers Surfer Rosa
years.p: Steve Albini starts [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]] with [[David Wm. Sims|c6c8a98f-9cfb-4fad-a657-880245ff15d3]] and [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]] of [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]], and engineers the [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]]' Surfer Rosa. Later come [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] and his Chicago studio, Electrical Audio.
years.xp: Albini refused producer credits and royalties, calling them an insult to the band, and charged indie bands low day rates. Over the next decade he recorded [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]], [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]], [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], [[PJ Harvey|e795e03d-b5d5-4a5f-834d-162cfb308a2c]] and [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s In Utero.

years.h: Durango records two Arsenal EPs from law school
years.p: Santiago Durango releases two EPs as Arsenal on Touch and Go while at law school and plays with [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]]. As a lawyer his clients included Touch and Go and Cynthia Plaster Caster; later he became an appellate defender in Ottawa, Illinois.

years.h: Pigpile puts the last London dates on record
years.p: Touch and Go releases the live album, recorded on the final 1987 tour, along with a single covering the Mary Jane Girls' In My House.

years.h: Cobain turns up at In Utero with a piece of Albini's guitar
years.p: At Nirvana's sessions in Cannon Falls, Minnesota, Kurt Cobain shows Steve Albini a chunk of the guitar Albini smashed at Big Black's last show. Albini recalled it for NME.
years.xp:
Albini remembered a kid in Seattle asking if he could take a piece of the guitar off the stage, and answering "go ahead its garbage now." Years later Cobain had it with him.

Cobain had chosen Albini after admiring his work on records by the Pixies and the Breeders, and Big Black's Atomizer.

years.h: Dave Riley has a stroke, first misreported as a suicide attempt
years.p: Dave Riley has a stroke in 1995 that at first is wrongly reported as a suicide attempt. He loses the ability to walk and later writes a blog called Worthless Goddamn Cripple.
years.xp:
Riley kept making music, with Algebra Suicide, Bull, Flour and in 2004 his own project, Miasma of Funk. In 2006 he published a book, Blurry and Disconnected: Tales of Sink-or-Swim Nihilism.

He declined to be interviewed for Rolling Stone's 2014 anniversary piece, saying only "Rolling Stone disgusts me."

years.cap: Steve Albini and the Roland at Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, Chicago, September 2006
years.h: Big Black plays four songs at Touch and Go's 25th birthday
years.p: Albini, Santiago Durango and original bassist Jeff Pezzati play Cables, Dead Billy, Pigeon Kill and Racer-X in Chicago. Albini said it would not happen again.
years.xp:
Albini explained that skipping it would have been an insult to Touch and Go, damning the label with faint praise. [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s touring left no time for real rehearsal, so the set stayed short, and stayed on the pre-Riley songs.

Riley, recovering from his stroke, wasn't asked to play. Albini: "I didn't want to put him in an awkward position of trying to play, but not being able to do it."

eras.title: Two deaths, five years apart
eras.text: Big Black's bassist and its founder died within five years of each other. Albini died with a new Shellac album days from release.

years.h: Dave Riley dies on Christmas Eve at 59
years.p: Big Black's bassist from 1985 to 1987 dies of squamous cell carcinoma in his throat and lungs, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: Ten days later, [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s To All Trains comes out on Touch and Go.
